questions.q: Who are the two main groups of people that interact with a bank?
questions.a: The two groups are savers and borrowers. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't grasped the basic "two-sided" nature of banking mentioned in the chapter.

questions.q: Why would someone choose to deposit money in a bank instead of keeping it in a metal box at home?
questions.a: A bank keeps money safe and pays interest, helping the savings grow. A wrong answer reveals the student thinks banks are just for hiding money, ignoring the growth aspect (interest).

questions.q: If you deposit ₹1,000 at a 5% interest rate, how much interest do you earn in one year?
questions.a: You earn ₹50. The calculation is 1,000 * 0.05. A wrong answer shows the student struggles with basic percentage applications in financial contexts.

questions.q: How does a bank benefit from the money deposited by savers?
questions.a: The bank uses those deposits to provide loans (borrowing) to others. A wrong answer indicates the student views the bank as a static vault rather than an active financial institution.

questions.q: Is it better for the economy if money sits in a jar or is deposited in a bank? Why?
questions.a: It is better in a bank because the money is put to work by being lent to borrowers who might use it for productive activities. A wrong answer reveals a failure to understand the "flow" of money in an economy.

questions.q: If you were a bank manager, why would you pay interest to the people who deposit their money?
questions.a: To encourage them to keep their money in the bank so the bank has enough funds to lend out. A poor answer fails to see the bank's need for a stable supply of money.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Banks act as financial bridges by ______ money from people who have extra savings (savers) and lending that money to people who need it for specific purposes (borrowers).
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have a piggy bank that is full, but your friend ______ money to buy a school uniform.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify who provides money to a bank and who receives it, explaining that the bank acts as a middleman that uses interest to manage this flow.
